found mixed_clocks at shop/cache.py:23 as high bug

findings_detail.description: set() now stores expiry as time.time() + ttl, but get() on line 17 still compares against time.monotonic(). The two clocks have unrelated epochs: time.time() is about 1.7e9 seconds since 1970, while time.monotonic() is typically uptime-scale (thousands to millions of seconds). So `time.monotonic() >= expires_at` is almost always False, and entries effectively never expire. The cache serves stale data forever and grows without bound.
findings_detail.fix_sketch: Use the same clock in both places: change line 17 to `time.time() >= expires_at`, or revert set() to time.monotonic(). Monotonic is preferable since it is immune to wall-clock adjustments.

meta.notes: set() uses time.time() but get() still compares against time.monotonic(): entries never expire.
